submissions.findingTextShort: PMID 12140984 is a forensic mass-burial paper and cannot support phosphatidylserine efficacy, safety, dosing, or grading.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 12140984, titled Identification of fragmented bodies of the killed from group burials, is a forensic medicine publication unrelated to phosphatidylserine supplementation, phospholipid biology, cognition, stress, or any phosphatidylserine intervention. The current published profile uses this source as the sole source in its canonical evidence object, so the edge is a direct source-identity failure and must be quarantined from all phosphatidylserine support.
submissions.usageContext: Source-integrity quarantine only; no phosphatidylserine intervention or proposition-equivalent evidence is present.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The entity/topic mismatch is direct. This draft finding documents the false source edge but does not itself alter canonical publication state, evidence grade, or recommendation eligibility.

submissions.findingTextShort: Phosphatidylserine is a phospholipid, so the live botanical/herb owner description is a taxonomy mismatch rather than an evidence property.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Phosphatidylserine is a phospholipid constituent of biological membranes and is not a botanical species or herb. The current runtime record is stored under herbs-detail and calls itself a botanical profile. Research should preserve the present workpack owner for shard-safe staging while flagging the taxonomy conflict for governed owner/type reconciliation; botanical classification must not be used to infer preparation, traditional use, or evidence propagation.
submissions.usageContext: Entity-taxonomy integrity finding only; no cross-system owner migration is performed in this research fragment.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Final canonical migration/alias behavior belongs to governed identity resolution. This finding must not silently create a duplicate compound owner or break existing routes.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2026 systematic review found controlled citicoline/PS cognition evidence in mental disorders heterogeneous, inconsistent, and insufficient for a general cognitive-enhancer claim.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2026 systematic review of 11 controlled studies of citicoline and phosphatidylserine-containing interventions in mental disorders found mixed and diagnosis-specific cognitive outcomes. ADHD studies included both positive and null findings, schizophrenia evidence showed a selective verbal-recall signal without global cognitive improvement, and mood/substance-use findings were mixed. Methodological limitations and high risk of bias led the authors to conclude that current evidence does not support these agents as established cognitive enhancers across mental disorders.
submissions.populationContext: Children, adolescents, and adults with ADHD, mood disorders, alcohol/substance-use disorders, or schizophrenia across 11 controlled studies.
submissions.usageContext: Review includes both citicoline and phosphatidylserine-containing interventions, including adjunctive/combination contexts; it is not proposition-equivalent proof for standalone phosphatidylserine in healthy adults.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Intervention heterogeneity, diagnosis heterogeneity, and high risk of bias prevent a universal cognition claim. Positive selective outcomes and null outcomes must coexist, and citicoline findings cannot be reassigned to phosphatidylserine. Draft-only pending registry and semantic attestation.

submissions.findingTextShort: A randomized soy-derived PS trial found no significant cognitive benefit at 300 or 600 mg/day in older adults with memory complaints.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A controlled trial randomized 120 adults older than 57 years with age-associated memory impairment to placebo, 300 mg/day soy-derived phosphatidylserine, or 600 mg/day soy-derived phosphatidylserine for 12 weeks. No significant between-group differences were found for the primary delayed-recall/recognition outcomes or other measured learning, memory, reaction-time, planning, or attention outcomes. This null formulation-specific trial is an important counterweight to older bovine-cortex phosphatidylserine studies and selected positive trials.
submissions.populationContext: One hundred twenty older adults with age-associated memory impairment or memory complaints.
submissions.usageContext: Soy-derived phosphatidylserine at 300 or 600 mg/day for 12 weeks; not interchangeable with bovine-cortex PS, PS-DHA, or PS/phosphatidic-acid complexes.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: A null soy-PS trial does not prove all phosphatidylserine formulations ineffective, but it materially limits universal cognition claims and undermines simple dose-response assumptions. Draft-only pending governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: A PS-DHA combination RCT reported a selected verbal-memory signal, which cannot be attributed to generic standalone phosphatidylserine.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 15-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 157 non-demented older adults with memory complaints tested phosphatidylserine containing omega-3 long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids attached to its backbone. Verbal immediate recall improved versus placebo, with additional favorable findings arising in post-hoc subgroups. Because the intervention was a PS-DHA formulation rather than generic standalone phosphatidylserine, the result supports only a bounded combination/formulation-specific cognition signal.
submissions.populationContext: Non-demented older adults with memory complaints; 157 randomized and 131 completed, with protocol exclusions from efficacy analysis.
submissions.usageContext: PS-DHA/omega-3 phosphatidylserine formulation for 15 weeks; combination identity must remain attached to the finding.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Post-hoc subgroup findings and formulation identity constrain generalization. The trial cannot establish efficacy of arbitrary soy PS, bovine-cortex PS, or a universal 100–300 mg/day regimen. Draft-only pending registry and semantic attestation.

submissions.findingTextShort: A randomized omega-3 phosphatidylserine stress trial found no significant main effect on stress measures, with favorable findings limited to subgroup analyses.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial assigned 60 healthy nonsmoking men aged 30 to 60 years to omega-3 phosphatidylserine or placebo for 12 weeks and assessed chronic stress plus responses to an acute laboratory stressor. The study reported no significant main treatment effect on stress measures, while selected favorable findings were confined to participants with higher chronic stress. The main-effect null result and subgroup restriction must remain visible.
submissions.populationContext: Sixty healthy nonsmoking men aged 30 to 60 years, with subgroup analyses by chronic-stress level.
submissions.usageContext: Omega-3 phosphatidylserine formulation for 12 weeks; not standalone generic phosphatidylserine and not evidence for treatment of an anxiety disorder.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Subgroup findings cannot overwrite the null overall treatment effect. Combination/formulation identity and healthy-volunteer context materially limit a generic stress-reduction claim. Draft-only pending governance.
